notes: Verdict assertion passes in both configurations (100%) — non-discriminating. Both with-skill and baseline produce a verdict.
Format-related assertions (conventional comments, structured output, triage pass) are the primary differentiators — baseline never produces these formats.
Substance assertions (architectural analysis, security, observability) show mixed results: baseline catches some (e.g., K8s backward compat) but misses others (security, observability in Prometheus).
With-skill reviews are faster on average (152s vs 216s) despite producing more structured output. The Prometheus baseline was an outlier at 384s (40 tool calls vs 20 for with-skill).
Token usage is comparable (~53K with-skill vs ~47K baseline). The skill doesn't significantly increase token consumption.
Both configurations found the same critical issues (nil pointer deref in Prometheus, duplicated validation in Terraform), suggesting the skill doesn't sacrifice depth for structure.
